page: UpCloud PREMIUM-80xCPU-512GB is a KVM-hypervised virtual server configured with 80 vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM. The underlying hardware features an AMD EPYC 9575F processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor configuration allocates 80 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. Memory density stands at 6.4 GB per core. The server includes 500 GB of local SSD storage and one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance type.

In benchmark evaluations, this server demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Geekbench multi-core score both rank in the top 10% of tested instances. Single-threaded performance is also strong, with Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core scores placing in the top 10% and top 25% respectively. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are highly developed, supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and VAES, reflected in a top-tier PassMark CPU encryption score. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high for cached small-block reads, while large-block uncached read and write operations maintain strong top-25% performance.

While raw computational throughput, software compilation, and decompression tasks perform in the top tier, the server exhibits limitations in memory-bound latency-sensitive tasks, with the PassMark memory score landing in the average tier. Additionally, large language model text generation speeds for both small and medium models fall into the bottom 25%, indicating that CPU-based LLM text generation is a significant bottleneck. Consequently, this server is highly suited for highly parallelized non-GPU workloads, including software compilation, large-scale web serving, database operations, and high-throughput data decompression, rather than active LLM text generation.

Built on KVM virtualization, it provides 80 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, paired with 500 GB of local SSD storage. The server delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, software compilation speeds, and cached memory bandwidth, ranking in the top 10% of benchmarks. It also exhibits strong performance in database operations and static web serving. However, memory latency benchmarks are average, and CPU-based LLM text generation is weak, ranking in the bottom 25%. This configuration is highly efficient for parallelized compute-heavy workloads, software development pipelines, and database hosting, offering a robust balance of high core density and substantial memory capacity.
